doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026

title: Starting with no procedures and losing the blues job
summary: With no procedures or staff, she was a one-man band; around then the old man's girlfriend fired her from the band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Was there a sort of, I’m going to use the word “triage” when a person was presented or came to you or was brought to the organization, was there an assessment like what do we need immediately and what could be the long-term plan for this person.

Honestly they just said, “Here are the keys to the office, you’re going to have to be a one- man band because we don’t have money to hire anyone else. And I looked through, there were tons of boxes and I looked through just to see – there wasn’t even a procedure on how to help. There wasn’t even a questionnaire. So it really was fabulous because you know what I neglected to tell you was that the old man in the train station that I played with got himself a girlfriend 15 years younger than him. It was his first woman in a long time. And she wanted to sing with the band. She fired me. So I was without my job, like I was without my blues. That was how I was feeding my children.
